title: EU TLS handshake failures — customer briefing & status copy (draft)
content:
Executive summary:

Between 2027-11-04 09:14 UTC and 2027-11-04 11:02 UTC, a subset of inference requests routed to EU regions experienced increased latencies and elevated TLS handshake failures (manifesting as 5xx errors and client-side connection resets). Customers with endpoints pinned to eu-west1 or eu-central1 saw a measurable increase in error rate and tail latency. No user data was exposed; this was a connectivity/handshake failure between control-plane services and inference nodes.

Impact (customer-facing):
- What customers saw: intermittent 5xx errors (TLS handshake failures) and slower responses when sending requests to models hosted in EU regions during the window above. Some requests were retried successfully; others failed and returned an error.
- Affected scope: ~3–6% of requests to EU inference pools (transient, concentrated during autoscaling bursts). Global hosted API customers using only non-EU regions were not affected. Dedicated deployments with on-prem private-control-plane were not impacted.
- Data integrity: No model outputs were leaked between tenants. No persisted customer data was compromised.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2027-11-04 09:12 — Rotation job launched as scheduled (control-plane cert rotation for EU mutual-TLS certs).
- 2027-11-04 09:14 — First errors detected by synthetic checks: spike in TLS failures for eu-west1. Pager alerted SRE.
- 2027-11-04 09:30 — Engineers identified correlation between cert rotation job and handshake errors during scale-out events.
- 2027-11-04 09:45 — Partial rollback of the rotation job and targeted restart of EU-side proxy pods initiated (mitigation step 1).
- 2027-11-04 10:12 — Handshakes began to stabilize for most traffic; error rate trending down.
- 2027-11-04 11:02 — Traffic returned to baseline; synthetic checks green.
- 2027-11-05 15:00 — Root-cause analysis kickoff; draft postmortem prepared.

Root cause (technical, customer-friendly):
An automated certificate rotation job updated intermediate certificates used by the control plane-to-inference-node mutual TLS channel. The rotation contained a sequencing bug: during concurrent scale-out events the control plane briefly presented an incomplete certificate chain to a small subset of newly spun inference proxies in EU regions. Those proxies rejected incoming connections until the chain was re-provisioned and pods restarted. The combination of an active scale-up (more proxies coming online) and the faulty sequencing produced a short window where TLS handshakes failed.

What we did (immediate mitigation):
- Rolled back the certificate rotation for EU regions to the prior validated bundle to restore stable handshakes.
- Performed targeted rolling restarts of the affected proxy pods to ensure they picked up the validated chain.
- Monitored synthetic checks and customer telemetry until error rates returned to baseline.
- Opened JIRA INFRA-7921 to track the fix and follow-up engineering work.

Permanent remediation (next steps):
- Fix the rotation orchestration to ensure certificate chain provisioning is atomic and ordered; add stronger pre-rotation validation. (Owner: eng-infrastructure, ETA: 2027-11-12)
- Add a canary stage to rotation jobs so new bundles are verified by a small canary pool under load before global rollout. (Owner: eng-sre, ETA: 2027-11-19)
- Improve autoscaling integration tests to simulate concurrent rotation + scale events and catch sequencing regressions. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime, ETA: 2027-11-26)
- Create a post-rotation healthcheck that validates TLS handshake success from multiple vantage points before marking rotation complete. (Owner: eng-observability, ETA: 2027-11-12)

Current status:
- Resolved: traffic returned to normal on 2027-11-04 11:02 UTC.
- Long-term fixes are scheduled (see remediation).

Customer-facing status page copy (suggested snippets) — short form (for status.redwood.ai):
- Update 1 (investigating): 2027-11-04 09:25 UTC — We are investigating elevated TLS handshake failures affecting traffic to EU inference regions. Users may see increased errors or latency. Our engineering team is working to identify the cause and mitigate impact.
- Update 2 (mitigating): 2027-11-04 09:50 UTC — We've applied an initial mitigation (rollback of recent certificate bundle change for EU regions) and are restarting a subset of proxy services to restore healthy TLS handshakes. Error rates are decreasing; we'll post another update when services return to baseline.
- Update 3 (resolved): 2027-11-04 11:05 UTC — Issue resolved. Certificate bundle rollback and targeted restarts have restored normal service levels. We are conducting a root cause analysis; customers will receive a follow-up summary and planned remediation.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (long form — suitable for email or partner brief):
Subject: Follow-up: Service disruption in EU regions on 2027-11-04 — what happened and next steps
Hello —

We want to follow up on the service disruption affecting EU-hosted inference traffic on 2027-11-04. Between 09:14 and 11:02 UTC we observed increased TLS handshake failures that caused intermittent errors and higher tail latency for some requests. The issue was caused by a certificate rotation sequencing bug in our control plane orchestration that impacted a small subset of newly provisioned proxy nodes during autoscaling.

What we did for you:
- Restored service via rollback and targeted restarts within 2 hours.
- Confirmed that customer data and outputs were not exposed.
- Initiated immediate remediation tasks and scheduled longer-term fixes (see bullet list above).

What we’re doing to prevent recurrence:
- Hardening the rotation process with atomic provisioning and canaries.
- Improving autoscaling + rotation testing coverage.
- Adding cross-region health checks to detect handshake regressions earlier.

If you saw customer impact or need assistance validating your flows, please reach out to your CSM or support@redwood.ai and reference INC-2027-11-04-EU-TLS. We can work with you on retry strategies, client-side backoff, or traffic routing recommendations while we complete remediation.

Credits and compensation:
- We will issue pro-rata service credits for measurable request failures resulting from this incident for impacted customers; customer-success will reach out to affected accounts with specifics and a simple claim process.

Suggested internal next steps (working doc items):
- Customer-success to triage affected accounts (top-50 EU customers) and prepare personalized emails. (Owner: Aisha Patel)
- Support to enable additional logs/packet captures for accounts that report persistent issues. (Owner: Marcus Chen)
- Engineering to complete INFRA-7921 and publish final postmortem. (Owner: eng-infrastructure)

Draft Q&A (for CSMs):
Q: Was my data exposed?
A: No — this was a TLS handshake failure between our control plane and inference proxies. No tenant data was leaked or persisted incorrectly.

Q: Why did rolling restarts help?
A: Restarts forced affected proxy pods to load the validated certificate bundle (the rollback package) and re-establish trusted chains with the control plane.

Q: Should I change my retry/backoff settings?
A: If you operate with aggressive immediate retries, consider brief exponential backoff (100–250ms initial with jitter) to reduce client-side amplified failures during transient network/control-plane events.
